title: No Measurable Benefit from Verifier‑Assisted Generate→Validate→Repair under Shared‑Initial Generation: A Preregistered Emulation Study
abstract: We preregistered and autonomously executed a paired emulation study (study‑cnd‑2026‑001) to test whether a verifier‑assisted generate→validate→repair pipeline increases oracle pass rates for LLM‑produced network configurations in vendor‑diverse emulated NetOps intent→configuration tasks. The frozen design used shared_initial_candidate generation semantics (one generator call per pair consumed by both conditions), declared model gpt‑5‑mini, a deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), and a repair budget ≤1 call/task. Execution produced 200 complete pairs (400 episodes), model_calls_used=200, and repair calls invoked=0. Results: baseline = 200/200 oracle passes; guarded = 200/200 oracle passes; absolute paired difference = 0.00 (paired bootstrap 95% CI [0.00,0.00], resamples=10,000, seed=1729); McNemar two‑sided p=1.00. The null result is design‑bound: every shared candidate passed the deterministic oracle, so the repair stage was never exercised. We release the full audited artifact bundle (preregistration, prompts, raw outputs, provider traces, validator traces, execution manifest and SHA‑256 digests) and provide artifact‑anchored recommendations for informative follow‑ups (independent generation semantics, calibrated difficulty, larger repair budgets, validator stress tests).

sections.introduction: Generative LLMs are being evaluated as intent→configuration agents for NetOps because they can translate human intent into device commands, scripts, and multi‑device workflows. Practical adoption requires operational correctness (safety, ordering, vendor idiom compliance). A prevalent mitigation architecture is generate→validate→repair: the generator proposes a candidate, a deterministic validator (oracle) checks objective properties, and a repair module attempts corrective generation when the oracle fails. Prior work motivates verifier‑assisted pipelines (constraint encoding, counterexample‑driven repair) but often lacks preregistered, artifact‑complete confirmatory comparisons. We preregistered study‑cnd‑2026‑001 to ask: "Does an automated verifier‑assisted generate→validate→repair pipeline increase the oracle pass rate (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline) relative to unconstrained generation across a stratified 200‑pair emulated NetOps task set?" Our contributions are (1) a fully preregistered, autonomously executed, artifact‑hashed paired experiment; (2) deterministic reconciliation and exact‑file hashing for complete audit; (3) the observed, artifact‑backed outcome and its causal design diagnosis; and (4) artifact‑grounded, actionable recommendations for follow‑up designs that allow the repair stage to be exercised.
sections.related_work: We situate this run among recent verifier‑ and constraint‑guided NetOps efforts (representative evidence in the supplied artifact bundle: MeshAgent constraint guidance (openalex W4416927413), NetConfEval intent→configuration benchmarks (openalex W4399629579), and verifier‑grounded program repair work (StruSpec; doi:10.31224/7995)). Those works motivate verifier assistance and repair loops; our study differs by preregistering the estimand, generation semantics, validator, and analysis executor, and by archiving every raw output and hash for deterministic audit. The literature shows both gains and failure‑mode dependence on generation semantics, validator expressiveness, and repair feedback quality; the present artifact bundle and manifest permit exact replay and targeted variant execution.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and frozen design: The study preregistration (study‑cnd‑2026‑001; SHA‑256 a8969ac01f3b1bb7585872c58a92f72d0752160dd4e6e01cbafbfe0d15073ad2) froze the primary estimand (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline), sampling plan (Npairs=200), generation semantics (shared_initial_candidate), declared generator (gpt‑5‑mini), deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1, and analysis executor (paired_binary_analysis_v1: paired bootstrap 10,000 resamples, seed=1729, plus exact McNemar two‑sided test). The initial master prompt that launched the autonomous run is archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba).

Task bank and stratification (artifact): The preregistered task manifest contains 200 paired tasks (execution/task_manifest.jsonl; manifest artifacts hashed). Tasks were stratified: four protocol buckets (BGP/OSPF/ACL/VLAN = 50 pairs each); within each protocol vendor allocations per preregistration were Cisco=17, Juniper=17, Arista=16 (per‑protocol), producing totals Cisco=68, Juniper=68, Arista=64; complexity split simple=100, complex=100. Each task entry encodes an intent, an initial and expected final state, required_sequence, constraints, and a reference answer (see representative scoring artifacts such as execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json, SHA‑256 eaf96aec12c3...).

Generation semantics and adapter: The frozen generation semantics shared_initial_candidate required a single generator call per pair; that single candidate was delivered to both the baseline (unconstrained) and guarded (verifier‑assisted) scorers. The declared generator was gpt‑5‑mini via adapter hosted_netops_gvr_v1; the model configuration artifact is execution/model_configuration.json (SHA‑256 1acce92558ed...). The execution manifest records model_calls_used=200 and maximum_model_calls allowed=400 (execution/execution_manifest.json).

Validator, repair, and scoring: The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) performs syntactic parsing, deterministic emulation of the intended configuration against the recorded initial state, and returns normalized_configuration, parsed_command_count, final_state, valid boolean, and violation codes; all validator traces and scoring JSONs are archived (execution/scoring/*.json). Repair was enabled in the design but in this run repair_calls_invoked=0 (repair_applied=false in every validator trace) because the validator never failed a shared candidate.

Analysis plan and reproducible artifacts: The primary analysis used paired_binary_analysis_v1: paired bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) and exact McNemar two‑sided test. All raw outputs, provider traces, scoring records, manifests and analysis artifacts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 7bc1bd2a..., analysis/condition_summary.csv SHA‑256 1cb072b4...) are archived with per‑file SHA‑256 digests for deterministic reconciliation. analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json verifies per‑file accounting and provider call counts.
sections.results:
Execution and raw outcomes (artifact‑anchored): The run completed per the preregistration: planned_episode_count=400, completed_episode_count=400, failed_episode_count=0, model_calls_used=200 (one shared generation per pair). Scoring summary (analysis/condition_summary.csv) shows baseline_success_count = 200/200 (100%); guarded_success_count = 200/200 (100%). The paired contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) is n11=200, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0.

Confirmatory inference (artifact: analysis/results.json): paired estimate = 0.00; paired bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.00,0.00] (bootstrap_resamples=10,000, seed=1729); McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00. These numbers directly match the archived analysis artifacts (analysis/paired_difference_figure.svg, analysis/analysis_log.jsonl).

Representative examples and validator traces: Representative scoring JSONs (e.g., execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json SHA‑256 eaf96aec12c3...) include the normalized_configuration, parsed_command_count, final_state dictionary, validator validity=true, and repair_applied=false. Several representative pairs and their shared candidates are archived as execution/responses/task-00000X-shared-initial.txt (example SHA‑256 values in the execution manifest). Deterministic_reconciliation.json confirms that every scoring record maps to a stored raw response and provider trace and that all internal counts are consistent (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json; SHA‑256 799b23b9...).

Operational diagnostics: repair_applied was false in all stored validator traces; repair budget was unused (repair_calls_invoked=0). The root cause is the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics plus generator behavior: the single shared candidate presented per pair passed the deterministic oracle in every case, producing a ceiling effect and preventing repair invocation. The artifacts record this (execution/execution_manifest.json, execution/scoring/*.json).
sections.discussion:
Design‑bound null result and causal diagnosis: The confirmatory null (no paired improvement) is a correct statistical consequence of the frozen design and the observed contingency: with identical passing shared candidates in both arms, there was no opportunity for the repair path to act. This is not evidence that verifier‑assisted repair can never help; it shows that under shared_initial_candidate semantics and the selected task bank plus generator behavior, repairs were never needed or invoked. The explanation is fully traceable in the artifact bundle (preregistration, execution manifest, scoring JSONs, analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json).

Implications for confirmatory NetOps evaluation: Two experimental design levers determine whether a repair stage can be exercised and thus measured: generation semantics and task difficulty/validator strictness. The present run fixes generation semantics to shared_initial_candidate and used a task bank whose sampled initial candidates (under gpt‑5‑mini) passed the deterministic validator. To measure repair efficacy, experiments should (a) allow independent sampling per condition (independent_per_condition) so baseline and guarded arms receive different generator draws, and (b) calibrate task difficulty (or adversarialize inputs) to produce a nontrivial baseline failure rate that leaves room for repair improvement. Both variant runs are directly reproducible from the archived prompts, task manifests, and adapter configuration; we document exact artifact paths and hashes so others can replay and modify the preregistration.

Reproducibility, auditability and best practices: This run demonstrates a reproducible pipeline pattern: freeze design in a machine‑readable preregistration (SHA‑256 a8969ac0...), archive the initial master prompt (provenance/master_prompt.txt SHA‑256 1872df1e...), run with deterministic validators, and publish raw outputs, provider traces, validator traces, scoring JSONs and per‑file SHA‑256 digests (execution/execution_manifest.json). Deterministic reconciliation (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json) is a minimal but powerful audit artifact that confirms counts, mapping, and absence of silent reruns. We recommend that future confirmatory NetOps studies include explicit preregistered generation semantics and explicit checks that repair stages are exercised with nonzero probability before relying on paired estimands.

Concrete artifact‑grounded follow‑ups (supported by the archived bundle): (1) Independent‑generation paired variant (change generation_semantics to independent_per_condition in a new preregistration) — expected to consume ≈400 generator calls and permits repair invocation when the generator occasionally produces failing candidates. (2) Difficulty calibration: augment the task manifest with higher‑difficulty tasks or boundary constraints so that initial candidates fail with measurable probability. (3) Larger repair budgets and iterative repair loops (>1 allowed repair call) while preserving provider traces and hashing. Each variant is implementable by editing the preregistration and reusing the archived prompt templates and task generators; the existing artifact layout provides exact seeds and representative tasks to bootstrap replication.

Threats to validity (artifact‑anchored): Internal validity — the shared_initial_candidate choice produced the ceiling effect and must be treated as a non‑neutral design choice; we preserved it as preregistered. Construct validity — the deterministic validator enforces specific emulation semantics and may miss production device nondeterminism; validator coverage flags are present in scoring JSONs to flag oracle_coverage_ambiguity. External validity — single declared model (gpt‑5‑mini) and synthetic emulation limit generalization. Conclusion validity — inference is exact for the frozen estimand but degenerate due to no discordant pairs; artifacts fully support this conclusion.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a fully archived paired emulation test of a verifier‑assisted generate→validate→repair pipeline under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Both baseline and guarded conditions achieved 200/200 oracle passes; the repair stage was never invoked; paired difference=0.00 (95% bootstrap CI [0.00,0.00]; McNemar p=1.00). The null result is explained by the preregistered generation semantics and the generator‑oracle interaction: because the single shared candidate per pair passed the deterministic oracle in every case, the repair path had no opportunity to act. The run demonstrates the necessity of matching generation semantics and task difficulty to the scientific estimand. We publish the full artifact bundle (preregistration, master prompt, prompts, raw outputs, provider traces, validator traces, execution manifest and per‑file SHA‑256 digests) so others can reproduce the run and execute recommended variants (independent generation, calibrated difficulty, larger repair budgets) that permit measurement of repair effectiveness.

The Research Director selected the broad topic family pre‑lock (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps); all substantive research actions reported here were performed autonomously after the autonomy lock.
- Preregistration: study id = study-cnd-2026-001; preregistration SHA‑256 = a8969ac01f3b1bb7585872c58a92f72d0752160dd4e6e01cbafbfe0d15073ad2. The preregistration froze the primary estimand, sampling plan, generation semantics (shared_initial_candidate), declared model, validator, repair budget, stopping rules, and analysis executor.
- Declared LLM and adapter: declared model = gpt-5-mini used via adapter hosted_netops_gvr_v1; model configuration artifact: execution/model_configuration.json (SHA‑256 = 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa). All provider call traces and raw responses are archived under execution/provider_calls/ and execution/responses/ with per‑file SHA‑256 digests recorded in execution/execution_manifest.json.
- Generation semantics (frozen): shared_initial_candidate (one generated candidate per pair provided to both baseline and guarded conditions). This preregistered choice produced model_calls_used=200 (one shared generation per 200 pairs) and is the proximate cause the guarded repair stage was never invoked (repair calls invoked = 0). The execution manifest records these counts and per‑file hashes (execution/execution_manifest.json).
- Validator and oracle: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 scored every candidate; representative scoring artifact: execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json (SHA‑256 eaf96aec12c30860a6fd70987289cc71104134a3330b99c7e024f244dbd35c1b). All validator traces are archived and hashed.
- Repair policy and budgeting: preregistered maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1; in this run repair calls invoked = 0 (artifact‑backed). Repair prompts would have been archived if used.
- Analysis procedures (frozen): paired_binary_analysis_v1; paired bootstrap 10,000 resamples (seed=1729) and exact McNemar two‑sided test. Confirmatory analysis artifacts: analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA‑256 7bc1bd2a42b5ac3f7adb61db47cf8dbe0472f678032abcd1e7c44f92ea2de71c) and analysis/condition_summary.csv (SHA‑256 1cb072b4db7c8e29212ef28b97baccb66a507a7c8b8ceaad35b7e84f7976a951).
- Execution and reproducibility: every prompt, model output, provider trace, validator trace, scoring record, manifest and analysis artifact is archived with SHA‑256 digests. Deterministic reconciliation confirms arithmetic and accounting consistency (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json; SHA‑256 799b23b9...).
- Human involvement: pre‑lock collaborative development and approval of the master prompt were performed by the Research Director. No human performed manual substantive editing of the manuscript after the autonomy lock. Pre‑lock development artifacts were not used as empirical evidence unless reproduced under the frozen post‑lock workflow.
- Deviations: none affecting the primary confirmatory analysis; model identifier did not change mid‑run; no pairs excluded; repair stage not triggered. The full execution manifest and per‑file SHA‑256 digests are included in the artifact bundle for audit.
limitations: The confirmatory conclusion applies only to the exact preregistered design (shared_initial_candidate semantics, single declared model gpt‑5‑mini, deterministic_netops_validator_v5, synthetic/emulated task bank of 200).

Shared_initial_candidate semantics created a ceiling effect: because the single shared generated candidate per pair passed the deterministic oracle for every task, the repair stage was never invoked (repair_calls_invoked = 0).
Emulation with a deterministic validator and synthetic tasks does not capture full production heterogeneity (real vendor device nondeterminism, image differences, runtime failures).
Single‑model execution limits generality across model families and instruction‑tuning variants; multi‑model generalization remains to be tested.
Repair budget was intentionally limited (≤1 call/task) by preregistration; richer iterative repair policies remain unexplored in this run.
Oracle blind spots remain possible; validator coverage diagnostics are archived and should be consulted when extending the study.
